debugging_computational_thinking.heading: Debugging as a Core Learning Outcome
workflow: 1. Observe the actual output vs. expected output
2. Identify error type (SyntaxError, IndentationError, NameError, TypeError, ValueError)
3. Read the traceback to pinpoint the file and line number
4. Inspect variable values in Thonny or using print statements
5. Test a targeted fix and verify program stability
common_errors_taught: SyntaxError: Missing colons, unclosed quotes, mismatched parentheses
IndentationError: Inconsistent tab/space indents or missing blocks
NameError: Variable typos or calling variables before assignment
TypeError: Concatenating strings with integers without str() conversion
ValueError: Converting non-numeric user input with int()
Logic errors: Off-by-one errors in range() or reversed boolean comparisons

responsible_ai_policy.heading: Responsible AI in Children's Python Education
responsible_ai_policy.approved_copy: AI tools are optional, teacher-supervised learning aids used exclusively to explain error messages and programming concepts. Children are never required to create external AI accounts or upload personal data.
guidelines: AI can assist with explaining confusing traceback error messages in plain language
AI can suggest conceptual analogies for difficult logic such as loops or parameters
Students must write, test, debug and explain 100% of their own code
AI-generated code cannot be submitted as student work
No child under 13 is ever asked to sign up for third-party AI services
Live instructor verification ensures authentic student understanding

child_safety_policy.heading: Child Privacy & Safe Beginner Coding Practices
child_safety_policy.approved_copy: Nova Skills enforces a strict child-safety standard. All programming is conducted in local desktop environments with zero mandatory public accounts, no external social forums, and private instructor assessment.
safeguards: No mandatory public GitHub, Replit, or social code sharing profiles
Work submitted as private source .py files reviewed directly by instructors
No personal child information (full names, schools, locations) collected or published
Safe programming practices: No external network requests or system-level scripts taught
Private end-of-course project showcase conducted safely for parents and educators

parent_showcase_model.heading: Parent Project Showcase & Authentic Assessment
parent_showcase_model.approved_copy: At the conclusion of the course, students present their original Python creations to parents and instructors, demonstrating runnable code and explaining the logic behind their decisions.
deliverables: Project 01: Python Turtle Creative Art (source .py + rendered visual artwork)
Project 02: Interactive Quiz or Number-Guessing Game (source .py + test run record)
Project 03: Original Python Game or Small Application (source .py + user documentation)
